To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the performance of MRSI for tumor detection is comparable to that of T2‐weighted MRI, and that (2) the performance can be improved by combining MRSI and T2‐weighted images in a multivariate classifier.

(1) the best performance in the classification of malignant and benign prostate tissue can be achieved with nonlinear methods that operate directly on magnitude spectra; (2) linear methods based on the magnitude spectra are less sensitive to the choice of a quantification algorithm and allow for biochemical interpretation of the results; and (3) linear methods based directly on the magnitude spectra achieve the same performance as the nonlinear methods and allow for biochemical and physiological interpretation of the results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable and efficient method for the automated evaluation of MRSI in prostate cancer diagnosis, which can be used for the development of an integrated diagnostic system.
the development of methods for the automated evaluation of MRSI of the prostate.
the development and application of novel statistical pattern recognition methods to the analysis of MRSI in prostate cancer.
